I found the exact root cause of the horizontal layout bug (the "wack x-axis")!

### The Root Cause:
In your index page structure:
* The main website template wraps sections in the `.content` class, which has `max-width: 600px` in `index.css`.
* Because `index.css` is loaded inside the HTML *after* the bundled timeline styles, it overrode the `.timeline-content` width of `100%` and `max-width: none`.
* This constrained the timeline's parent width to exactly `600px`, while its internal SVG scaled down to fit the narrow space. Because the SVG was forced to `760px` vertical height in CSS, it stretched the layout vertically while squishing the horizontal axis down by 60%, resulting in the extremely skinny/compressed appearance in the screenshot!

### The Solution:
I updated **`timeline.css`** to guarantee the timeline overrides the 600px layout width using `!important`:
```css
.timeline-content {
  max-width: none !important;
  width: 100% !important;
  box-sizing: border-box;
}
```
This successfully restores the timeline component to its intended expansive full-width horizontal layout, restoring correct year spacing, label positioning, and preventing any horizontal squishing!

Please reload your local browser at `http://localhost:1234` to see the timeline spread out beautifully!
